The Arab Kings.

And whenever they found them in bands,
they slaughtered them.
And the territories of the Turks were filled with plunder from the Franks,
so that talents of silver were sold like lead in Melitene.
And those of the Franks who escaped
and returned to the coast of the Pontic Sea,
the Greeks mixed lime with flour and fed it to the Franks;
and when they ate it,
they fell in heaps and died.
Now the king of the Germans escaped with only three counts, and came to Jerusalem,
and he prayed and received a blessing from the Holy Sepulchre.
And after he had rested for some days,
he came against Damascus with ten thousand horsemen and sixty thousand foot soldiers.
Now the Turks and the Arabs amounted to about one hundred and thirty thousand foot soldiers,
apart from horsemen.
And when the Franks saw that there was no strength in the Arabs and Turks, even though they were numerous,
they took courage and advanced until they encamped by the rivers
and in the midst of the gardens.
Then Mu'in, the ruler of Damascus, when he saw that his hope was completely cut off,
sent secretly to the king of Jerusalem,
and seduced him with words and with gold,
saying: "Two hundred thousand dinars,"
—all of them copper, plated with Egyptian gold.
And likewise to the ruler of Tiberias
he sent fifty thousand of this counterfeit gold,
which later on, when it was passed,
was examined and exposed.
And concerning this gold:
although I have encountered five different histories of the Arabs,
I have not found it in this narrative,
but only the blessed Mar Michael recorded it.
Now the great king of the Germans,
when he perceived the treachery,
abandoned Damascus
and returned to his country in great sorrow.
And this was the evil end of that great army.
Now the king of Sicily,
when he understood the treachery of the Greeks, became enraged,
and came against the city of Thebes, captured it, and laid it waste,
and destroyed the Greeks who were in it with the sword.
And he did likewise also to Adrianople and to Philippopolis,
and he also came to Constantinople
and devastated its entire territory.
And at this time, when Leon the Armenian, ruler of Cilicia, died in Constantinople,
